---
title: "Deterministic primitives"
---

Primitives are one-call helpers that register a hook for a common pattern. They
target the right events, count fires, and suppress echo for you, so a fired message the agent repeats back doesn't re-trigger the hook. The deterministic primitives decide the outcome with a regex, an AST walk, or a predicate, no model call. For the LLM-backed primitives, see [LLM Hooks](llm-hooks.qmd).

## Pick a primitive

Start from what you want to enforce.

- For a Bash command, [`block_command`](#block_command) denies it,
  [`warn_command`](#warn_command) flags it without stopping it, and
  [`rewrite_command`](#rewrite_command) swaps it for a better one before it runs.
- Advise the agent when conditions or accumulating signals fire, go to [`nudge`](#nudge).
- Require something done before the agent finishes, go to [`gate`](#gate).
- Check a Python edit against a rule, go to [`lint`](#lint).
- Flag only what an edit changed, go to [`diff_lint`](#diff_lint).

Each primitive accepts `tests={...}` mapping an `Input` to a `Block`, `Warn`, or
`Allow` expectation. Run them with `uvx capt-hook test`. The
[primitives reference](../reference/primitives.qmd) holds every full signature.

::: {.callout-tip title="Prefer declarative"}
A custom predicate belongs in a [`CustomCondition.check()`](conditions.qmd#write-a-custom-condition)
and fires through a declarative `nudge`, `gate`, or `hook`. Reach for an `@on` handler only when you
need threaded session state, a per-event message computed at runtime, an LLM evaluation, or
command-line AST queries.
:::

## block_command {#block_command}

Block a Bash command before it runs. Pass a token list and captain-hook builds a
whitespace-tolerant regex, so `["git", "stash"]` matches `git stash` and `git stash pop`.

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Block, Input, block_command

block_command(
    ["git", "stash"],
    reason="Use the team's VCS workflow for shelving changes",
    hint="Commit a WIP change instead",
    tests={
        Input(command="git stash"): Block(),
        Input(command="git stash pop"): Block(),
        Input(command="git status"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

Pass a raw string when you need a precise pattern, such as
`r"git\s+push\s+--force(?!-)"` to block a force-push while allowing `--force-with-lease`.

## warn_command {#warn_command}

Warn on a command without blocking it. The agent sees the message and keeps going.

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Input, Warn, warn_command

warn_command(
    ["python", "-c"],
    message="Prefer `uv run mtest` over raw `python -c`",
    tests={
        Input(command="python -c 'print(1)'"): Warn(),
        Input(command="uv run mtest"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

## nudge {#nudge}

Advise the agent when a condition holds or when signals accumulate. A plain nudge with
`only_if` fires once on the next matching tool use. Add `signals` to fire only after the
transcript crosses a weighted threshold, which catches a pattern like repeated retries.

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Input, Signal, Signals, Warn, nudge

nudge(
    "You keep retrying. Narrow the failing test before running it again.",
    signals=Signals(
        patterns=[
            Signal(pattern=r"let me try again", weight=2),
            Signal(pattern=r"retry", weight=1),
        ],
        threshold=3,
        window=10,
    ),
    tests={
        Input(transcript=[
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "let me try again"},
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "retry the suite"},
        ]): Warn(pattern="failing test"),
        Input(transcript=[{"role": "assistant", "content": "all green"}]): Allow(),
    },
)
```

A nudge with `signals` defaults to `PostToolUse`; without them it defaults to
`PreToolUse`. See [Signals](signals.qmd) for the scoring model.

## gate {#gate}

Require something done before the agent stops. A gate is a blocking nudge on the
`Stop | SubagentStop` events, so it holds the turn open until the work is complete.

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Block, Input, RanCommand, Waiting, gate

gate(
    "Run the tests before stopping.",
    skip_if=[Waiting(), RanCommand(r"uv\s+run\s+mtest")],
    tests={
        Input(transcript=[
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "edited the parser"},
        ]): Block(pattern="Run the tests"),
        Input(transcript=[
            {"role": "assistant", "content": "ran `uv run mtest`, all green"},
        ]): Allow(),
    },
)
```

A gate is the same as `nudge(message, block=True, ...)`.

Stop gates are wait-aware by default. Give a gate no `skip_if` and it skips while the
agent waits on background work such as a running `Workflow`, an async sub-agent, or a
`ScheduleWakeup` loop, then re-fires once that work resumes. Pass any `skip_if` and that
default switches off, so include [`Waiting()`](../reference/conditions.qmd) yourself, as
the example in this section does.

## lint {#lint}

Check a Python edit against a rule. captain-hook infers the mode from the check's first
parameter. A `str` parameter receives the file content; an `ast.AST` parameter receives
each walked node. The check returns violation strings spliced into `{violations}`.

```python
import ast
from collections.abc import Iterator

from captain_hook import Allow, Input, Warn, lint


def bare_excepts(node: ast.AST) -> Iterator[str]:
    if isinstance(node, ast.ExceptHandler) and node.type is None:
        yield f"line {node.lineno}: bare except"


lint(
    bare_excepts,
    message="Bare except clauses silently swallow errors: {violations}",
    trigger="except",
    tests={
        Input(tool="Edit", file="app.py", content="try:\n    f()\nexcept:\n    pass\n"): Warn(pattern="bare except"),
        Input(tool="Edit", file="app.py", content="try:\n    f()\nexcept OSError:\n    pass\n"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

Lints fire on `PostToolUse` for `Edit` and `Write` of `.py` files, and skip test files.
The `trigger` substring is a cheap pre-filter, so captain-hook parses only when the
source contains it.

## diff_lint {#diff_lint}

Flag only what an edit changed. The check takes the pre-edit and post-edit AST and
returns violations for the delta, so a rule fires on a newly added construct without
nagging about code the edit left alone.

```python
import ast

from captain_hook import Allow, Input, Warn, diff_lint


def added_prints(pre: ast.AST, post: ast.AST) -> list[str]:
    def prints(tree: ast.AST) -> set[int]:
        return {
            node.lineno
            for node in ast.walk(tree)
            if isinstance(node, ast.Call)
            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)
            and node.func.id == "print"
        }

    return [f"line {n}" for n in sorted(prints(post) - prints(pre))]


diff_lint(
    added_prints,
    message="This edit added a print() call: {violations}",
    tests={
        Input(tool="Edit", old="x = 1\n", content="x = 1\nprint(x)\n"): Warn(pattern="added a print"),
        Input(tool="Edit", old="print(1)\n", content="print(1)\nx = 2\n"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

`diff_lint` fires on `Edit` of `.py` files by default. For declarative AST rules scoped
to the change, see [Style Rules](styleguide.qmd).

## rewrite_command {#rewrite_command}

Swap a Bash command for a better one before it runs, instead of blocking and making the
agent retry. The hook fires on `PreToolUse` for Bash and replaces the command, surfacing
`note` as context so the model sees the substitution. It has two forms.

The **regex form** takes a `pattern` and a `replace` template and rewrites matching
commands with `re.sub`. Use it for a fixed textual swap.

```python
from captain_hook import Allow, Input, Rewrite, rewrite_command

rewrite_command(
    r"^cat\s+(\S+)$",
    r"ccx read \1 --full",
    note="Rewrote cat to ccx read",
    tests={
        Input(command="cat README.md"): Rewrite(pattern="ccx read README.md"),
        Input(command="grep foo bar.py"): Allow(),
    },
)
```

`Rewrite(pattern=...)` matches a substring of the rewritten command, so it survives any
absolute-path prefix the rewrite adds.

The **conditional form** takes `to=`, a callable that maps the event to its new command.
The hook fires on every Bash command, gated by `[Tool("Bash"), *only_if]`. Your `to`
callable receives the event, reads `evt.command` for the raw string or `evt.command_line`
for the parsed form, and returns the rewritten command, or `None` to block with `block`.
Reach for it when the decision depends on parsed structure, not a fixed textual swap.

```python
from captain_hook import Block, Input, Rewrite, rewrite_command


def to_safe_push(evt):
    cl = evt.command_line
    if not cl.q.runs("git", "push") or not cl.q.contains_token("--force"):
        return evt.command  # not a bare force-push; leave it untouched
    if cl.q.contains_token("--force-with-lease"):
        return None  # already lease-guarded but flagged here; block to be explicit
    return evt.command.replace("--force", "--force-with-lease", 1)


rewrite_command(
    to=to_safe_push,
    block="Use --force-with-lease, not a bare force-push.",
    note="Rewrote --force to the lease form.",
    tests={
        Input(command="git push --force origin main"): Rewrite(pattern="--force-with-lease"),
        Input(command="git push --force --force-with-lease"): Block(pattern="lease"),
    },
)
```

A `to` callable that returns `None` blocks with `block`; otherwise it returns the command
string, rewritten or unchanged to leave it alone. `note` may itself be a callable computed
from the event when the conditional form needs a per-command message. Passing both
`(pattern, replace)` and `to=`, or neither, raises `TypeError`.
